chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Do not lodge the women in the rooms (upper chambers), and do not teach them writing, and teach them the spinning (of wool/thread), and [teach them] Surah Al-Nur.'

key_terms.الْغُرَفِ: Upper rooms or chambers, often implying a separate or elevated living space for women.
key_terms.الْكِتَابَةَ: Writing, specifically the skill of script and literacy.
key_terms.الْمِغْزَلَ: The spinning spindle, referring to the craft of spinning thread or wool.
key_terms.سُورَةَ النُّورِ: Surah Al-Nur (Chapter 24 of the Quran), known for its verses on modesty and family law.

ai.seo_question: What are the specific domestic and educational instructions for women in Shia hadith regarding housing and skills?
ai.summary: In the context of Al-Kulayni’s *Al-Kafi*, this hadith reflects the socio-historical norms of early Islamic society, where 'ghuraf' (upper rooms) symbolized seclusion and 'kitabah' (writing) was often associated with administrative or public roles. Shia scholars interpret the recommendation to teach 'mighzal' (spinning) and Surah Al-Nur as a balance between domestic utility and spiritual grounding, emphasizing modesty and religious literacy over broader intellectual pursuits.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Do not lodge the women in the room and do not teach them the writing, and teach them the spinning, and Surah Al-Noor (Chapter 24)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfafiy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘You must not lodge women in a chamber, do not teach them writing (that would lead to unlawful behavior), but teach them the spinning wheel and Chapter 24 of the Quran.’”
